rubrics.criterion: The per-domain reconciliation flow in the Cloudflare record path delegates each record creation, update, and deletion site (including the duplicate-handling and stale-record deletion phases of its loops) to one single owning record-mutation implementation per operation, instead of embedding copies of the endpoint construction at the loop sites.
rubrics.rationale: The reconciliation flow is the product's main hot path and held six embedded copies of three endpoint operations; whether every mutation site delegates is the core of this instance's resolution.

rubrics.criterion: Zone-record listing and name-filtered listing are each expressed by exactly one production implementation, and the reconciliation flow's existing-record lookup obtains its records through those implementations (directly or through higher layers) rather than through a re-implemented listing/filtering/request sequence.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's deepest flattening unreeled a three-level chain (request plumbing, listing, filtering) into the reconciliation flow in a stacked shape; restoring the layering here is the heart of the task.

rubrics.criterion: Shared HTTP request/response handling (URL resolution, auth application, optional request body, send, status check, error reporting, response deserialization) exists as one owned implementation that the record and WAF operations call, with none of the service-layer operations re-implementing it inline.
rubrics.rationale: The flattening embedded the transport primitive at multiple sites across two flows; a single transport owner exercised by all operations is required for the layering to be real.

rubrics.criterion: The WAF maintenance flow delegates its three steps — locating the configured list, querying its items, and removing managed item ids — to single owning implementations (including the conditional/early-return lookup), instead of embedding those step bodies in the cleanup method.
rubrics.rationale: All three maintenance steps were absorbed into the conditional cleanup method, one of them into a match-scrutinee position; delegating all three is a distinct concrete obligation of this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The legacy-mode update path delegates per-detected-IP record commits to one single-entry commit implementation, and the legacy batch update delegates its per-IP work to the per-IP update implementation (including the loop and its commit calls) rather than embedding either body.
rubrics.rationale: Both delegation levels of the legacy path were absorbed with receiver/argument adaptations; the batch update contained a two-level embedded stack and must delegate level by level.

rubrics.criterion: Provider dispatch delegates to the per-provider detection implementations, in particular the local-provider arm calling the local-socket detection routine rather than embedding its body, and each remaining provider arm still routes to its own detection implementation.
rubrics.rationale: The flattening reached a third subsystem (detection); a repaired dispatch preserves per-provider specialization via delegation.

rubrics.criterion: No production method anywhere in the update pipeline still contains a statement block that re-implements the whole body of another production method in place of calling it.
rubrics.rationale: Guards against partial repairs that fix the flagship flow but leave a less-visited site (a WAF step, an arm, a legacy level, an update-vs-delete phase) still flattened.

rubrics.criterion: The restored delegating call sites pass their surrounding values (record ids, payload objects, item id collections, formatter/notifier handles, dry-run and reporting sets) directly through parameter positions, without keeping caller-side single-use adapter locals that existed only as scaffolding around the embedded copies.
rubrics.rationale: The flattening introduced per-site hoisted adapters (verb bindings, stringly id views, payload references, id slices); a real consolidation absorbs them into parameter passing or removes them.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor does not leave the two update paths inconsistent: the modern Cloudflare record flow and the legacy-mode path must both be fully delegated, with neither path retaining embedded operation bodies while the other is cleaned up.
rubrics.rationale: Both paths were flattened in the same pass; repairing one path and not the other is a plausible incomplete outcome specific to this instance.

rubrics.criterion: No orphaned duplicate of a replaced operation remains: every operation has exactly one implementation, and no formerly-embedded body survives as a second (production-unreferenced) copy beside the implementation the caller now uses.
rubrics.rationale: The flattening left bypassed definitions behind each embedded copy; a completed repair removes such double definitions rather than swapping which copy is called.

rubrics.criterion: Every service-layer operation that the reconciliation, cleanup, legacy, and detection flows rely on is genuinely reachable from production entry points through the restored delegation, with no operation left defined but uncalled.
rubrics.rationale: The flattening stranded several operation definitions without production callers; connectivity of the restored layering is an observable completion fact.

rubrics.criterion: Record-identifying arguments keep their intended roles at every delegating call: zone ids and record ids (and WAF account ids and list ids) are not exchanged with each other anywhere in the restored flows.
rubrics.rationale: The affected signatures take adjacent same-typed id parameters; a swap compiles silently but maintains the wrong endpoints, so this concrete regression must be checked rather than assumed away.

rubrics.criterion: Dry-run behavior and no-op reporting are unchanged: dry-run record runs still perform no network mutations, emit the same informational messages, and the per-record no-op suppression or reporting behavior still prevents repeated identical updates from being reported as changes.
rubrics.rationale: The embedded copies interleaved dry-run guards and suppression bookkeeping with copied plumbing; reassembly must not lose or double those behaviors.

rubrics.criterion: Local-address detection and WAF cleanup keep their observable semantics: per-family local detection still binds an ephemeral socket, connects to the same well-known targets, and applies the same global-address filtering and warnings; WAF cleanup still removes exactly the managed item ids and nothing else.
rubrics.rationale: Detection and WAF maintenance are user-visible behaviors exercised by the suite; plausible but wrong reassembly (per-item removal requests, dropped global-address filter, changed probe targets) would silently change what the tool does.
